name: Scenario-based hedged allocation
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Positioning Before Event Repricing
caseLead: Scenario-based allocations seek to benefit when geopolitical or policy developments change the outlook for particular sectors, currencies or commodities before prices fully adjust. The opportunity persists because most investors react to an event after it has happened, while ETFs make a precise exposure easy to trade and few portfolios review scenario probabilities frequently.
caseRest: The main risk is that an event develops differently from the expected scenario, causing both the selected exposures and their hedges to lose value. During broad liquidations, assets that normally offset each other, such as equities, gold and long-dated Treasuries, can fall at the same time. The estimated 9.2% annual return therefore comes with 9.0% volatility and a 12.0% worst fall, and the hedges reduce these losses without removing them.
figNote: Each card shows the highest closing level of the VIX during the episode. The VIX measures the volatility that S&P 500 options price in for the next 30 days: it has averaged about 19 over the long run, while readings above 30 signal market stress.

events.title: US downgrade lifts gold and Treasury prices
events.text: Standard & Poor's downgrade of the US credit rating in August 2011 lifted the VIX to a 48 close, yet Treasury prices and gold both rose. The strategy gained because its hedges in Treasury and gold funds offset falls in equity positions.

events.title: Yuan devaluation triggers a global equity sell-off
events.text: China's devaluation of the yuan in August 2015 raised fears about global growth, and the VIX closed at 41 in the sell-off. The strategy lost because emerging market and commodity positions fell together while the hedges were too small.

events.title: Brexit vote weakens sterling and lifts safe havens
events.text: The UK vote to leave the European Union in June 2016 lowered sterling by about 8% against the US dollar in a day, and the VIX closed at 26. The strategy gained because gold, yen and Treasury hedges rose while equities recovered within weeks.

events.title: Covid cash rush breaks down the hedges
events.text: The March 2020 sell-off became a rush for cash that lifted the VIX to an 83 close. The strategy lost because gold and Treasury hedges fell alongside equities as investors sold liquid assets to meet margin calls.

events.title: Ukraine invasion lifts oil and lowers bonds
events.text: Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine pushed Brent crude above $120 a barrel in March and lifted the VIX to a 36 close. Results were mixed because energy and commodity funds gained while Treasury hedges lost value as inflation expectations rose.

events.title: US tariffs test Treasury and gold hedges
events.text: The April 2025 US tariff announcement lifted the VIX to a 52 close, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose about half a percentage point within a week. Results were mixed because gold funds gained while Treasury hedges lost value.

instrument: Sector, country, gold, Treasury and currency ETFs; held for days to months; reviewed weekly
rules: Exposure added when the scenario engine assigns an event a probability above 30%; hedges sized to the main risks of that event; positions reduced as the outlook changes
costs: Estimated ETF bid-ask spreads, commissions and fund fees deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from event exposure to portfolio hedges

legs.purpose: Earns from assets most exposed to the leading scenario
Hedges a sharp fall in growth
Limits losses if scenarios fail together

entry: Scenario probability above 30% and an ETF with a clear link to the event
size: Set to a 9% annualised volatility target; single ETF capped at 15%
exit: Position reduced when the scenario probability halves, or after 60 days
stop: Event positions closed if the portfolio falls 6% from its peak
marketWatch: The probabilities that Rehyn's scenario engine assigns to the leading events, and the cost of hedging them, are the main indicators because they show how much of each event is already priced. Elections, summits, sanctions decisions and central bank meetings matter most when they change the likelihood of an event that affects several asset classes at once.

favourable.heading: Events follow the leading scenario
favourable.text: An event that follows the leading scenario favours the strategy because the exposed assets move as expected while hedges cost little. After the UK vote to leave the European Union in 2016, gold, yen and Treasury holdings rose while equity losses reversed within weeks.

favourable.heading: Safe haven assets keep their role
favourable.text: Hedges that rise when equities fall favour the strategy because they offset losses on event exposures. In August 2011, both Treasury prices and gold rose after the US credit rating downgrade.

favourable.heading: Hedging costs stay low
favourable.text: Low option and hedging costs favour the strategy because protection reduces losses without absorbing much of the return. Implied volatility was low for most of 2017, so hedges were inexpensive and the portfolio kept most of its gains.

adverse.heading: Hedges fall with equities
adverse.text: Falling hedges hurt the strategy because gold and Treasury funds are meant to offset equity losses. In March 2020, investors sold both to raise cash while the VIX closed at 83.

adverse.heading: Inflation lifts bond yields
adverse.text: Rising inflation expectations hurt the strategy because Treasury hedges fall in price when yields rise. In 2022, the Ukraine war raised energy prices and Treasury funds lost value alongside equities.

adverse.heading: Events surprise the scenarios
adverse.text: Events that differ from the scenarios hurt the strategy because positions are sized for the wrong risks. In August 2015, the devaluation of the yuan caused emerging market and commodity positions to fall together.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's estimated peak-to-trough change in value during each event, using the ETF exposures and hedges that the scenario engine would have selected at the time. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in equities, oil, gold, interest rates and currencies, which are then applied to the strategy's current ETF holdings and hedges.
altTitle: Where Else Can Investors Find Returns from Event Risk?

related.why: Buys index put options. Bears the premium cost, paying in calm markets and gaining in a crash.
Trades rate, currency and commodity futures on macro trends. Bears the risk that policy changes reverse the trend.
related.cue: Trend signals instead of scenario views

related.why: Trades oil option prices around supply events. Bears time decay when an event passes without a price move.
related.cue: Oil events through options, not ETFs
